notes: Heating Up round (2026-10-07): the Pyroblast line reads the Heating Up buff (400625), which exists only once the build has taken the talent (Pyroblast then Heating Up, from the middle of the Fire tree), so it is declared inert for the truncated low-level builds. Adapted from the fork's shared mage default (ui/mage/apls/p1.apl.json), which is the Fire branch of a package that falls back to Frostbolt for non-Fire specs. Its Fireball and Frostbolt references were stale ranks (10) where the build's current top ranks are 12 (25306) and 11 (25304) respectively; Frostbolt is dropped entirely since this file is Fire-specific and never falls back to it. Fire Blast is added on cooldown as a free extra nuke per community guides, which the shared preset omitted. Fix round 1 re-gated the Improved Scorch stack check from the client's Fire Vulnerability id (22959) to 12873, the id sim/core/debuffs.go's ImprovedScorchAura hardcodes. Fix round 3 read that as a permanent engine gap -- 'the engine's Improved Scorch debuff aura is created only by the raid's own debuff toggle, never by this mage's own Scorch casts' -- deleted the Scorch-stacking mechanic entirely, and made Combustion an unconditional cooldown. The fix-round-3 re-review (fix-round-3-rereview.md) showed that premise false: sim/mage/talents.go's applyImprovedScorch() (called from every mage's normal ApplyTalents(), whenever Talents.ImprovedScorch != 0) wires mage.ImprovedScorchAuras to the *same* core.ImprovedScorchAura(12873) constructor the raid toggle uses, and sim/mage/scorch.go's ApplyEffects -- run by every Scorch rank -- rolls a 33/66/100% (by talent rank) chance per cast to Activate/AddStack that exact aura on the current target. The mage's own Scorch casts do stack 12873, gated behind the Improved Scorch talent Fire mages actually take; this line restores that mechanic (Combustion popped once the target is fully stacked, Scorch keeping the five stacks up and refreshed before they fall off, Fireball as the filler once the debuff is up), matching the cited guide's Fire rotation and mage-arcane's own precedent of naming a talent-dependent line that a no-talent smoke build cannot resolve. Under this bare smoke build (no talents at all) mage.ImprovedScorchAuras is never populated, so every auraIsActive/auraNumStacks/auraRemainingTime reference against 12873 on the current target finds no such aura, core.GetAPLAura logs its own 'No aura found' validation warning, and the whole nil-filtered `or` gate on the Scorch line collapses to nil -- which APLAction.IsReady reads as always-true, so Scorch is recast on every global under this one build. That is the build lacking the talent, not a defect in the gate; recorded as a written smokeBuildWarnings entry (mage-fire, {SpellID: 12873}), the same shape as the hunters' zero-SwingSpeed auto-shot artifact. Every other rank named here is checked against the spellconst of the newest client build in builds/; 12873 stays outside that check (ENGINE_AURA_IDS) since it is an aura the engine registers under its own id, confirmed present at sim/core/debuffs.go:624-637, not a client spellconst entry. Rotation-accuracy program fix round (2026-09-28): this file never actually declared 12873 in its own `inert` array despite the notes above describing it as exactly that kind of known, deliberate, talent-gated unresolved id -- the ladder's own strict check (unlike the earlier smokeBuildWarnings assertion this paragraph references) has no separate 'id only appears inside a condition' exemption, so it still flagged {SpellID: 12873} as a violation below the level the truncated build's talent walk reaches Improved Scorch's row (levels 10 and 20). Declared inert below to match what the notes already said was true. Rotation-accuracy program, wand-weaving addition (2026-09-28): Shoot (5019) is declared inert for the same shape of reason -- this build's item table has no wand with required_level <= 10, so the level-10 rung equips nothing in the ranged slot and core.RegisterShootSpell never registers the spell there. From level 20 on it resolves and fires heavily (up to 99 percent of top casts at level 30 on this bare, no-consumes, no-buffs ladder character). Scorch filler round (2026-10-07): the raid preset's Improved Scorch debuff LOWERED a level-60 mage-fire by about 4 percent (see design/reviews/2026-10-07-fire-external-scorch.md). The engine is right (the two Improved Scorch writers share one aura and five stacks raise Fire damage taken by exactly 15 percent); the rotation was the cause. With Fireball as the filler, the only Scorch casts were the five that rebuilt the debuff each time it lapsed (about 26 of them in 180 seconds, since the refresh gate waits for 1.5 seconds remaining and a 3 second Fireball skips past it), and those casts were the mage's most mana-efficient damage; an external debuff removed them and the mage fell back to the weaker Fireball filler. Measured with paired seeds on the level 60 band character, Scorch as the filler beats Fireball by 10 to 12 percent at 180 and 300 seconds and 5 to 8 percent at 60, at levels 40, 50 and 60, and is neutral to positive with the external debuff. Fireball stays as the line before Scorch is trained. Theorycraft audit (casters.md X1, F1, F4): the wand line is an out-of-mana fallback now that a wand shot cannot start inside a GCD. A Fireball filler re-measured on the fixed engine, with Fireball's DoT critting, still ran out of mana and lost to Scorch, so Scorch stays the filler; the raid talent search moved nothing past the 1 percent bar. Sim-accuracy round 4 (design/reviews/2026-11-01-sim-audit-round4/casters.md): Clearcasting used to stay up for its whole 15 seconds, so this list never ran out of mana; spent by one damage spell, it ran dry about 49 seconds into a 180 second fight. Evocation below 5% mana was added and measured +17% on the level-60 raid character (thresholds of 5, 10 and 20% within error of each other). Gating Fire Blast on the mana pace, dropping it, or a Fireball filler above the mana pace each measured at or below this list. Guide rewrite (2026-11-02): Pyroblast is cast 6 s before the pull and lands at it, as Fire mages open in game; about +1.5% with raid buffs and +0.4% without (a pre-pull Fireball measured +1.1% and +1.4%).

expected_idle.reason: Pyroblast is cast only on three stacks of Heating Up, a talent two rows below Pyroblast in the Fire tree; the ladder build at level 30 has spent on Pyroblast but not yet on Heating Up, so the line correctly never fires there.

Fireball is the filler until the build takes Heating Up (level 30), and on the raid build, which takes Arcane Blast; the leveling build from 30 fills with the Heating Up-gated Scorch line and reaches Fireball only if Scorch cannot be afforded, which it can whenever Fireball can.
Arcane Missiles is cast only on a Missile Barrage proc, a talent only the raid build takes; the leveling ladder never procs it.
Arcane Blast is a talent only the raid build takes (the Arcane tier-two pick at the end of the raid order); the leveling ladder never knows it.

engineering_notes.1: Fix round 4: tracks the engine's own debuff id (12873, sim/core/debuffs.go's ImprovedScorchAura), which the mage's own Scorch casts stack when Improved Scorch is talented (sim/mage/talents.go's applyImprovedScorch, sim/mage/scorch.go's ApplyEffects) -- restored after fix round 3 mistakenly treated this as impossible. 12873 is not in spellconst (it is an engine-side aura id, not a client spell), a known, deliberate exception for this one condition.
engineering_notes.2: Fix round 4 restored the mechanic (see top-level notes) but left the refresh gated on a bare `or` of auraIsActive/auraNumStacks/auraRemainingTime against 12873 -- under this build's no-talent smoke run those three all fail to construct (GetAPLAura's aura.Get() is nil before the talent ever registers ImprovedScorchAura on the target), newValueOr filters every nil sub-value out of its list, and an `or` with zero surviving vals returns nil, which APLAction.IsReady reads as always-ready -- so Scorch, not 'inert', became 100% of every cast and Fire Blast/Fireball never fired once Scorch was learned. Fix round 5 wraps the same `or` in `and(auraIsKnown(12873), or(...))`: auraIsKnown (sim/core/apl_values_aura.go) never returns nil, only true/false, because it just reads whether the Aura object exists on the target rather than requiring an active instance -- and applyImprovedScorch (sim/mage/talents.go:341-343) registers that object via NewEnemyAuraArray the moment the talent is present, independent of stacks. Once the inner `or` goes nil under no talent, newValueAnd's own nil filter (same mechanism as `or`, sim/core/apl_values_operators.go) drops it and the `and` degrades to the single surviving auraIsKnown value, which is false without the talent, so the whole line is skipped and the priority list falls through to Fire Blast then Fireball -- proven with the scratch castSet at level 60 untalented.
engineering_notes.3: Scorch filler round (2026-10-07): the Fireball line became a Scorch (rank 7) filler line, with Fireball (rank 11) kept after it for levels below Scorch's 22. The refresh gate (fix round 5's and(auraIsKnown, or(...)) line) is unchanged and still runs ahead of Pyroblast and Fire Blast; it now only matters for the opening stack-up and after a long Pyroblast, because every filler Scorch renews the debuff.
engineering_notes.4: Sim-accuracy round 21 (design/reviews/2026-11-05-sim-audit-round21/mage.md F-S1): the Scorch filler line is gated on auraIsKnown(400625), Heating Up, which both Fire orders take at 30. Below it Fireball is the filler: on the bare band-20 ladder at levels 22, 25, 28 and 29 (10,000 iterations, seeds 1 and 50001) the Fireball filler beats the Scorch filler by 0.4 to 1.1 percent, because rank 1 and 2 Scorch do about a fifth less damage per mana than Fireball rank 4 and 5 and the band-20 mage runs out of mana. From 30 Heating Up and Improved Scorch turn it round by about 10 percent, so the 60 line is unchanged. The Improved Scorch stack line still casts Scorch at 27 to 29.
engineering_notes.5: Sim-accuracy round 21 (design/reviews/2026-11-05-sim-audit-round21/mage.md X4): Evocation (12051) trains at 20 and the engine no longer registers it below that level; the ladder level-gates the line through idLearnLevelOverrides (sim/request/ladder.go) and sim/internal/spellranks' singleTierLevelOverrides, so it is not declared inert.
engineering_notes.6: Sim-accuracy round 22 (design/reviews/2026-11-05-sim-audit-round22/mage.md F1, from the MythicSim comparison): the raid build moved to Accelerant 5/5, Missile Barrage 2/2 and Arcane Blast (Arcane 14, Fire 34, Frost 3; Wand Specialization, Arcane Resilience, Flame Throwing and Arcane Meditation, none of which acts on a boss, pay for it; Burning Soul 2/3 stays). On it Fireball is the filler: the Fireball line, the gap Scorch before Fire Blast and the Arcane Blast line are gated on spellIsKnown(Arcane Blast), which only the raid build takes, and the Scorch filler on its complement. Missiles on Missile Barrage reads the proc. The Improved Scorch refresh moved from 1.5 s to 5 s left because a 3 s Fireball skipped past the old window. Raid 60, frozen BiS, 10,000 iterations: +1.75% Alliance, +2.05% Horde at seeds 1 and 50001.
engineering_notes.7: Sim-accuracy round 23 (design/reviews/2026-11-05-sim-audit-round23/mage.md F1): the level 60 build moved to the raid build's Fire tree, Missile Barrage and Arcane Blast, with Wand Specialization 2/2 for two Improved Channeling ranks (2301052001000/55500201230133031/003). Arcane Blast lands at 57 on the ladder, so the gated lines (Fireball filler, gap Scorch, Arcane Blast) run at 57 to 60 and the Scorch filler at 30 to 56; at 33 to 55 a Fireball filler loses 6 to 26% to Scorch on the new ladder, at 57 and 60 Scorch loses 4%. Notes 9 and 10 name the levels.

sources.label: Warcraft Tavern: Classic Fire Mage DPS rotation

priorityList.notes: Evocation when you are nearly dry and more than 30 seconds of the fight remain. It is an 8 second channel at +1500% mana regeneration on an 8 minute cooldown, so it comes once a fight: spend your mana gem from 28 and a mana potion first, and at 60 a Demonic Rune too. Inside the last 30 seconds the mana comes back too late to spend, so keep casting.

Combustion once the boss carries 5 Improved Scorch stacks, with your on-use trinkets and your damage racial if your race has one. Every Fire hit then adds 10% crit until three non-periodic crits land, and each Scorch or Fire Blast crit is an Ignite and a Heating Up stack. Give a fresh tank a few seconds of threat first.

Scorch to build Improved Scorch to 5 stacks, or to refresh it with 5 seconds or less left. A Fireball takes 3 seconds or more, so a later refresh can land after the stacks are gone. The debuff only boosts your own Fire damage, so every Fire mage keeps their own stacks, and a Scorch that misses adds none. With one point of Improved Scorch a Scorch lands a stack only one time in three, so build them only on a mob that lives a minute or more; from the second point they pay on anything that lives 20 seconds.

Pyroblast only on 3 stacks of Heating Up, when it is a 1.5 second cast. Every Fire Blast hit and every Scorch, Fireball or Fire Blast crit adds a stack, and the cast spends them all. At 6 seconds, or on 1 or 2 stacks, it loses to your filler.

Fire Blast every time it is off cooldown: it is instant, and once you have Heating Up every hit is a stack. With both points of Improved Fire Blast it is a 6 second cooldown. Once you have Improved Scorch, the Scorches that build your 5 stacks go ahead of it, and once you have Heating Up so does a Pyroblast on 3 stacks. In raid gear it costs more mana for its damage than Scorch, Fireball or Pyroblast, but skipping it to save mana costs more damage than the mana buys.

Arcane Missiles the moment Missile Barrage procs, while the proc is up. It is free and takes half the time, a missile every half second. Every Fireball has a 20% chance to give it with both ranks of Missile Barrage, half that with one, and once you have Arcane Blast it procs it 40% of the time.

Arcane Blast whenever its buff has dropped, once, then back to Fire. Each cast adds 12% of your Intellect as spell damage to every spell you cast for 18 seconds and takes Incineration's crit. Once you have Missile Barrage, each cast has a 40% chance to light it. A second cast while the buff is up doubles its cost for one more stack, so let it fall off first.
Scorch when Fire Blast is back before a Scorch would finish. A 3 second Fireball would hold your next Fire Blast, and its Heating Up stack, until the cast ends.

From Heating Up at 30 until Arcane Blast at 54, Scorch is the filler, not Fireball. You land about two Scorches in the time of one Fireball, so you roll twice the crits for Ignite and Heating Up, and every cast keeps your Improved Scorch stacks rolling.

Fireball is the filler once you have Arcane Blast, which the leveling build takes at 54. Five points of Accelerant make it a 3 second cast, each one has a 20% chance to make your next Arcane Missiles free through Missile Barrage, and with Arcane Blast's spell damage up it does more over a boss than Scorch. Its crits feed Ignite and Heating Up like any other Fire crit.

Until you have Heating Up, Fireball is the filler. At the ranks you have in the 20s it does more damage per point of mana than Scorch, and mana is what runs out first, so Scorch waits for Improved Scorch and then only builds and refreshes the stacks.

Shoot only when you are out of mana and waiting on a gem, a rune or Evocation. A wand shot cannot start during the global cooldown, so it never fits between spells; once you are shooting, the first shot fires half a second after you press it and the rest come at the wand's speed until you cast again.
